doc.title: Eddie Alley interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: The two songwriters of 'I Left My Heart in San Francisco'
summary: Two quiet men came to the Savoy nightly; years later he learned they wrote the Tony Bennett hit.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: And she liked somebody down to earth. These guys might try to put her on, and so, here’s another story though. There’s two guys that used to come in the place every night, two guys, and sit in the corner. And they said they were songwriters. I said don’t pay any attention to them, I said that’s nice. So about five years later, when Tony Bennett had that song “I Left My Heart in San Francisco,” I found out these are the guys that wrote the song. If I had known that I would have shaked hands with them.
See if you could get on the record.
But I didn’t pay any attention to these two guys.
But these are the guys that wrote “I Left My Heart in San Francisco,” and he just added that to his — you heard the story about that — he just added that song onto whatever his record date was.

It wasn’t in his record date at first, he just threw that in because he needed another song. And it became the number one song. And these are the two guys that wrote it. I used to see them all the time, came in there. If I’d have known it—little things like that.
